steps: Read the axis labels carefully — what quantity is on each axis?
For distance-time: gradient = speed; flat = stationary
For speed-time: gradient = acceleration; area under graph = distance
Read values by drawing lines from one axis to the graph and then to the other axis
Check units — make sure your answer uses the right units
method_card.title: How to Interpret Real-Life Graphs
method_card.content:
Real-life graphs use axes to represent measurable quantities such as distance, time, speed, temperature, or cost.

Distance-time graphs: The gradient represents speed. A steeper line = faster speed. A horizontal line means the object is stationary. Speed = distance ÷ time (the gradient of the line).

Speed-time graphs: The gradient represents acceleration. The area under the graph represents the total distance travelled. A horizontal line means constant speed; a downward slope means deceleration.

Conversion graphs: Straight lines that convert between units (e.g. miles ↔ kilometres, £ ↔ €). Read across from one axis, up/down to the line, then across to the other axis.

Container-filling graphs: The shape of the graph depends on the cross-section of the container. A wider section fills more slowly (shallower curve); a narrower section fills faster (steeper curve).
method_card.example:
A distance-time graph shows a cyclist who travels 12 km in 30 minutes, rests for 10 minutes, then returns home in 20 minutes.

Speed going: 12 km ÷ 0.5 hours = 24 km/h

Rest: 10 minutes — horizontal line at 12 km

Speed returning: 12 km ÷ ⅓ hour = 36 km/h

The return is steeper because the cyclist is faster.

gold.display: Find the total distance travelled for the entire journey shown in the speed-time graph.

misconceptions.message: Triangle 1: ½ × 4 × 20 = 40 m. Rectangle: 8 × 20 = 160 m. Triangle 2: ½ × 4 × 20 = 40 m. Triangle 3 (decel): ½ × 4 × 10 = 20 m. Wait — re-read the graph: 0→4s accel (triangle ½×4×20=40), 4→12s constant (8×20=160), 12→16s decel to 10 (trapezium ½×(20+10)×4=60), 16→20s decel to 0 (triangle ½×4×10=20). Total = 40+160+60+20 = 280 m.

gold.display: A speed-time graph shows: 0–5 s accelerating from 0 to 15 m/s, 5–15 s constant at 15 m/s, 15–20 s decelerating to 0. Find the total distance.

misconceptions.message: Triangle 1: ½ × 5 × 15 = 37.5 m. Rectangle: 10 × 15 = 150 m. Triangle 2: ½ × 5 × 15 = 37.5 m. Total = 225 m.

gold.display: A distance-time graph shows a runner covering 400 m in 50 seconds. For the first 20 seconds they ran at constant speed, covering 200 m. What was their speed (m/s) in the first 20 seconds?
A speed-time graph shows constant acceleration from 5 m/s to 25 m/s over 8 seconds. What is the acceleration?

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = (25 − 5) ÷ 8 = 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5 m/s².

gold.display: A speed-time graph is a triangle: speed increases from 0 to 30 m/s over 12 seconds, then instantly drops to 0. What is the total distance?

misconceptions.message: Area of triangle = ½ × 12 × 30 = 180 m.

bronze.display: The distance-time graph shows a journey. How far had the person travelled after 20 minutes?

misconceptions.message: Read up from 20 minutes on the x-axis to the line, then across to the y-axis: 6 km.

bronze.display: Using the same journey graph, for how many minutes was the person stationary?

misconceptions.message: The flat section (no distance change) runs from 20 to 30 minutes. Stationary time = 30 − 20 = 10 minutes.

bronze.display: A car travels 60 km in 2 hours at constant speed. What is its speed in km/h?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 km/h.

bronze.display: A conversion graph shows that 5 miles = 8 km. How many km is 10 miles?

misconceptions.message: 10 miles is double 5 miles, so double 8 km: 16 km.

bronze.display: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line mean?

misconceptions.message: A horizontal line means the distance isn't changing — the object is stationary.

bronze.display: A walker covers 4 km in 1 hour. What is their speed in km per minute?

misconceptions.message: 4 km ÷ 60 minutes ≈ 0.067 km/min (to 3 d.p.).

bronze.display: On a speed-time graph, what does the area under the graph represent?

misconceptions.message: The area under a speed-time graph always gives the distance travelled.

bronze.display: A bus travels at a constant speed of 40 km/h for 3 hours. How far does it go?

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time = 40 × 3 = 120 km.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a car's journey. What is the acceleration during the first 10 seconds?

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = (20 − 0) ÷ 10 = 2 m/s².

silver.display: A distance-time graph shows a cyclist covering 15 km in 30 minutes. What is the speed in km/h?

misconceptions.message: 30 minutes = 0.5 hours. Speed = 15 ÷ 0.5 = 30 km/h.

silver.display: A speed-time graph shows constant speed of 12 m/s for 20 seconds. What is the distance?

misconceptions.message: Area = rectangle = 12 × 20 = 240 m.

silver.display: A speed-time graph shows a car accelerating from 0 to 30 m/s in 6 seconds. What is the acceleration?

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = (30 − 0) ÷ 6 = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 m/s².

silver.display: On a distance-time graph, a steeper line represents:

misconceptions.message: A steeper gradient means greater speed — more distance per unit time.

silver.display: A speed-time graph shows a car decelerating from 25 m/s to 5 m/s in 10 seconds. What is the deceleration?

misconceptions.message: Deceleration = (25 − 5) ÷ 10 = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 m/s². (Give as a positive value.)

silver.display: A conversion graph shows 1 inch = 2.54 cm. How many cm is 8 inches?
